# Find max exit time
max_time = max(exit_time for exit_time, _, _, _ in ants)

# Among those with max_time, determine which ant is last
# If an ant moving right has max_time, it starts at position L - max_time
# If an ant moving left has max_time, it starts at position max_time
# The last ant will be the one with the farthest starting position from the exit it's heading to,
# and if both directions have same max_time, the one that started closer to the opposite end will exit last.

candidates = [ant for ant in ants if ant[0] == max_time]

else:
    # Two ants (one from each direction) finish at same time.
    # The one that was originally closer to the far end will be last.
    # For L direction, exit at pos 0, so larger pos => later.
    # For R direction, exit at L, so smaller pos => later.
    # Among candidates, sort by position descending for L, ascending for R.
    # Actually we compare the actual positions:
    # The one that had to travel farther is last.
    # For L: pos gives distance.
    # For R: L-pos gives distance.
    # So compare pos for L and L-pos for R.
    # But both have same exit_time, so:
    # L-ant: time = pos
    # R-ant: time = L - pos
    # Same time => pos (L) = L - pos (R) => pos(L) + pos(R) = L
    # The one with smaller starting position (if L) or larger starting position (if R) will exit last.
    # Actually simulate: If both reach exit at same moment, the one that started farther from its exit
    # will cross the exit line later by infinitesimal? They exit simultaneously, but problem expects one.
    # Typically the one moving left whose position is larger exits last.
    left_candidates = [c for c in candidates if c[2] == 'L']
    right_candidates = [c for c in candidates if c[2] == 'R']
    if left_candidates and right_candidates:

        right_pos = right_candidates[0][1]
        # The ant that started farther from its exit will be last
        # L ant distance = left_pos, R ant distance = L - right_pos
        if left_pos > L - right_pos:

import sys

def solve():
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    if not data:
        return

    it = iter(data)
    out = []

    # Input format assumed:
    # T
    # n l
    # D p   (n lines)
    # ...
    #
    # D is 'L'/'R' or any equivalent left/right word starting with L/R.
    #
    # Output:
    # "The last ant will fall down in X seconds - started at Y."
    # or
    # "The last ant will fall down in X seconds - started at Y and Z."
    #
    # This is the classic "Ants" identity-swap problem.

    t = int(next(it))
    for _ in range(t):
        n = int(next(it))
        length = int(next(it))

        ants = []
        positions = []
        for _ in range(n):
            d = next(it)
            p = int(next(it))
            dir_sign = -1 if d[0].upper() == 'L' else 1
            ants.append((p, dir_sign))
            positions.append(p)

        # Sort ants by initial position.
        ants.sort()
        positions.sort()

        # Compute fall events if ants pass through each other:
        # left-moving ant at p falls at time p on left side
        # right-moving ant at p falls at time length - p on right side
        events = []
        for p, d in ants:
            if d == -1:
                events.append((p, 0))          # 0 = left side
            else:
                events.append((length - p, 1)) # 1 = right side

        events.sort()

        # Assign original identities using order preservation:
        # when an ant falls from left, it's the leftmost remaining label;
        # from right, it's the rightmost remaining label.
        left_idx = 0
        right_idx = n - 1

        last_time = events[-1][0]
        last_ids = []

        i = 0
        while i < n:
            time = events[i][0]
            same = []
            while i < n and events[i][0] == time:
                same.append(events[i])
                i += 1

            fallen = []
            for _, side in same:
                if side == 0:
                    fallen.append(positions[left_idx])
                    left_idx += 1
                else:
                    fallen.append(positions[right_idx])
                    right_idx -= 1

            if time == last_time:
                last_ids.extend(fallen)

        last_ids.sort()

        if len(last_ids) == 1:
            out.append(
                f"The last ant will fall down in {last_time} seconds - started at {last_ids[0]}."
            )
        else:
            out.append(
                f"The last ant will fall down in {last_time} seconds - started at {last_ids[0]} and {last_ids[1]}."
            )

    sys.stdout.write("\n".join(out))

if __name__ == "__main__":
    solve()
